key_insight: Optimizing the cavity shape for capillary auto-ejection can generate centimeter-scale liquid drops that relax faster after ejection, making them suitable for short microgravity windows.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design rule for passive drop generators in drop-tower experiments, where drops must become nearly spherical within seconds.
method: Used a parabolic cavity filled with a fixed liquid volume and minimized the initial free-surface area.
Ran smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to compare relaxation times across cavity shapes.
Tested a modified shape with a shallow central depression to further accelerate relaxation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based evaluation showing that the minimum-area parabolic shape gives the shortest relaxation time within that family, and that a shallow central depression improves it further.
watch_item: The best-performing depression shape may be sensitive to fabrication tolerances and liquid properties, so experimental validation is needed before deployment.
paper_title: Rapid generation of relaxed centimeter-sized drops by capillary auto-ejection
